Project Description:
DocuMint is a developer productivity tool designed to bridge the gap between rapid software development and maintainable codebases. Writing comprehensive documentation is a universally disliked chore for developers, often resulting in legacy systems and hackathon prototypes that are difficult to read, scale, or hand over to other team members. DocuMint automates this bottleneck entirely.

The application functions as a highly fast, lightweight developer pipeline. When pointed at a local Python file or directory, it uses Python’s native code-parsing ecosystem to map out the codebase's architecture. It isolates functions that lack descriptive documentation, analyzes their inner logic, and generates context-aware, accurately typed docstrings. By integrating static code analysis with intelligent automated inference, DocuMint automatically updates source files with uniform, production-ready documentation—saving developer hours and keeping codebases completely clean without stalling feature velocity.

Project Title 

SynapseOps: Autonomous Multi-Agent Infrastructure Self-Healing Engine via MCP

Problem Statement 

Modern distributed microservice and edge environments experience catastrophic cascading failures where traditional static alerting frameworks (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana) cause massive alert fatigue. When a failure occurs, human Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) must manually parse disconnected logs, trace network dependencies, and execute rollbacks. This manual root-cause analysis drives Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) into hours, leading to significant financial loss and systemic downtime.

Problem Statement Description 

SynapseOps solves this by replacing passive alerting with an active, localized multi-agent orchestration framework that automates the entire detection-to-remediation pipeline.

[System Anomaly] ──> [FastAPI Webhook] ──> [Orchestrator Agent] │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ [Log Analyzer Agent] [Blast Radius Agent] [Action Executor Agent] (Vector Search/Semantic Parsing) (Graph DB Dependency Mapping) (MCP Tool Execution/Rollback) Key Architectural Pillars Edge-Native Ingestion: A lightweight daemon monitors system metrics and streaming logs at the OS level. Upon detecting an anomaly (e.g., a memory leak, critical error spikes, or thread deadlocks), it pushes a compressed payload via an optimized protocol to a high-performance backend. Multi-Agent Orchestration: The backend initializes a directed-acyclic graph (DAG) agent workflow. Instead of a single monolithic LLM call, specialized agents collaborate concurrently: Log Analyzer Agent: Connects to log streams to extract semantic errors, matching them against historical failure contexts using a high-performance vector database. Blast Radius Agent: Queries a localized graph representation of the infrastructure to map upstream and downstream dependencies, identifying the true root cause versus symptomatic failures. Action Executor Agent: Utilizes the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to safely execute context-aware tools (e.g., container isolation, dynamic traffic rerouting, service restarts, or Git rollbacks) within secure sandboxed environments. Latency Mitigation: To meet real-time production demands, the system implements rigorous semantic caching on the orchestrator level, bypassing the LLM entirely for previously resolved, identical failure patterns and dropping remediation latency from minutes to milliseconds.

Unlike traditional monitoring dashboards, ResponSync enables predictive, explainable, and data-driven disaster management, helping authorities act proactively while keeping citizens informed through an interactive geospatial interface.

Project Title: Smart Bike Fall Detection and Real-Time Emergency Notification System Using IoT
Problem Statement: Road accidents involving two-wheelers often leave riders unable to seek immediate help, especially in isolated areas. Project Description: The proposed project is an IoT-Based Bike Fall Detection and Emergency Alert System designed to enhance the safety of two-wheeler riders. A manual reset button is provided to cancel false alarms before emergency alerts are transmitted. The proposed system offers a low-cost, cloud-connected solution for real-time accident detection, live monitoring, and rapid emergency response.

Project Description: SnakeID is a machine learning-based image classification system that identifies common Indian snake species — starting with the "Big Four" venomous snakes (Spectacled Cobra, Common Krait, Russell's Viper, Saw-scaled Viper) and 5–6 common non-venomous look-alikes — from a photo. The hackathon demo focuses on software-only image classification with a simple interface for uploading a snake photo and receiving species identification plus antivenom guidance; hardware integration (e.g., an on-site camera device for remote clinics) is scoped as a stretch goal.

Project Title: SAKSHI: A Tamper-Evident Procedural Accountability Layer for Sensitive Legal Cases in India
Problem Statement: Sensitive legal cases—such as POCSO and murder investigations—pass through multiple independent agencies, including the police, hospitals, forensic laboratories, Child Welfare Committees, and courts. Existing platforms like CCTNS, eCourts, and ICJS support record management and information sharing across these agencies. As a result, delays may go unnoticed, handovers remain unverified, and procedural inconsistencies are often identified only after they have affected the investigation or judicial process. The gap is not information sharing—it is procedural accountability.
Project Description:
SAKSHI is a tamper-evident procedural accountability platform designed for sensitive legal cases. Instead of replacing existing government systems such as CCTNS, ICJS, and eCourts, it works alongside them as an additional accountability layer. The platform securely tracks every stage of a case, verifies inter-agency handovers through dual sign-off, monitors legally mandated timelines, and maintains a tamper-evident audit trail to improve transparency and accountability.

Our MVP focuses on POCSO cases because they follow well-defined legal procedures and timelines, making them suitable for demonstrating the platform's capabilities. However, the core framework is designed to be adaptable, allowing it to support other sensitive case types, such as murder investigations, by configuring their specific workflows, stakeholders, and procedural timelines.

Project Title: PLC SENTINEL :- THE AUTONOMOUS LOGIC INTEGRITY & RECOVERY SYSTEM
Problem Statement: PLC Sentinel: Autonomous Logic Integrity Monitoring, Threat Detection & Self-Recovery Framework for Industrial Control Systems
Project Description:
PLC Sentinel: Autonomous Logic Integrity Monitoring, Threat Detection & Self-Recovery Framework for Industrial Control Systems
Project Description
PLC Sentinel is an AI-powered cybersecurity and industrial automation solution designed to protect Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) from unauthorized logic modifications, cyberattacks, accidental programming errors, and system failures. It continuously monitors PLC logic in real time, verifies the integrity of ladder logic and control programs, and detects any deviation from the approved baseline using intelligent anomaly detection.
When suspicious logic changes, malware, ransomware, insider threats, or communication anomalies are identified, the system immediately isolates the affected PLC, alerts operators through a centralized dashboard, and performs autonomous recovery by restoring the last verified and trusted PLC program from a secure backup repository. This minimizes production downtime and prevents unsafe industrial operations.
PLC Sentinel also provides predictive threat analytics, audit logs, version control, and compliance reporting, enabling industries to maintain secure, reliable, and resilient Industrial Control Systems (ICS). The framework integrates with SCADA, IIoT devices, and modern industrial networks to deliver continuous monitoring, cyber resilience, and operational continuity.
Designed for Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0, PLC Sentinel transforms conventional PLC security into an intelligent self-healing defense system that ensures uninterrupted manufacturing, enhances operational safety, reduces maintenance costs, and safeguards critical infrastructure against evolving cyber threats. It is suitable for industries such as manufacturing, power generation, oil & gas, water treatment, pharmaceuticals, food processing, and smart factories.

Project Title: Smart Civic Connect – An AI-Powered Platform for Civic Issue Reporting, Routing, and Resolution Tracking
Problem Statement: Citizens frequently encounter civic issues such as potholes, garbage accumulation, water leakage, and broken streetlights, but lack a structured way to report them to the concerned authority. Complaints raised through calls or informal channels are often lost, misrouted, or left unaddressed, with no visibility into resolution progress. Duplicate reporting of the same issue by multiple citizens further fragments departmental effort and delays action. The result is inconsistent resolution, poor accountability, and declining citizen trust in civic administration.
Project Description:
Smart Civic Connect is a web/mobile platform that allows citizens to report civic issues by submitting a photo, location, and a brief description of the problem. An AI-based classification engine analyzes the complaint description and automatically routes it to the appropriate department (Road, Water, Garbage, Electricity, Sewage, etc.), with the citizen able to confirm or override the assignment before submission — eliminating the guesswork of identifying the right authority.
To reduce redundant reporting, the system uses AI-driven similarity analysis to detect existing unresolved complaints in the same location, flagging likely duplicates and allowing citizens to upvote an existing report instead of filing a new one — giving departments an accurate, consolidated view of complaint frequency and public impact.
Every complaint is assigned a unique tracking ID and progresses through defined status stages — Pending, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved — visible to the citizen throughout. Department staff access a dedicated dashboard showing only their assigned complaints, intelligently ranked by urgency, and update status with a resolution photo as proof of closure, reinforcing transparency and accountability.
An auto-escalation mechanism flags complaints left unaddressed beyond a defined timeframe, alerting senior authorities to prevent issues from stalling indefinitely. A map view consolidates all open complaints in a given area, supporting faster departmental oversight and planning.
By combining AI-driven intelligence with a lean, practical architecture, Smart Civic Connect closes the loop between citizen and department — transforming informal, untracked complaints into a transparent, accountable, and efficiently managed resolution process ready for real-world municipal adoption.

Most existing inspection systems rely on supervised deep learning models that require thousands of manually labeled images for every product type and defect category. Whenever a new product, component, or production line is introduced, manufacturers must collect new datasets, annotate defects, and retrain models, resulting in significant delays, increased costs, and reduced operational efficiency.

A major limitation of current systems is their inability to detect previously unseen or rare defects. Since these models learn only from labeled examples, they often fail to identify novel anomalies, making quality assurance less reliable in dynamic manufacturing environments. Furthermore, traditional inspection solutions typically provide only a simple pass/fail result or a defect bounding box, leaving engineers to manually analyze defect characteristics, identify recurring patterns, and determine corrective actions.

Large manufacturing enterprises may have the resources to maintain product-specific AI models, but small and medium-sized industries often cannot afford the time, expertise, or infrastructure required to continuously develop and retrain inspection systems.

With the rapid adoption of Industry 4.0, there is a growing need for an intelligent, explainable, and scalable visual inspection platform that can adapt to new products without extensive retraining. Such a system should not only detect anomalies but also provide meaningful explanations, visualize defects interactively, analyze inspection results across production batches, and assist engineers in making faster, data-driven quality decisions. Addressing these challenges will improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce inspection costs, minimize product wastage, and accelerate the transition toward autonomous and intelligent quality assurance.
Project Description:
OmniInspect AI is an autonomous visual inspection platform designed to revolutionize industrial quality control through zero-shot artificial intelligence, explainable computer vision, and interactive digital twin technology. Unlike conventional inspection systems that require thousands of labeled defect images and product-specific model retraining, OmniInspect AI leverages foundation models to inspect previously unseen products with minimal setup, enabling faster deployment across diverse manufacturing environments.

The platform combines CLIP for zero-shot visual understanding and Segment Anything Model (SAM) for precise defect localization to automatically inspect every component within a production batch. Each detected anomaly is transformed into a unique DefectDNA—a digital fingerprint representing its visual characteristics, including shape, texture, location, severity, and semantic features. These fingerprints are stored and compared with historical inspection records to identify recurring defect patterns and support faster root-cause investigation.

To improve interpretability and operator efficiency, OmniInspect AI generates an interactive 3D Digital Twin of the inspected production tray. Every component can be individually selected, rotated, and explored, allowing engineers to visualize defect regions, compare them with reference components, review AI-generated explanations, and analyze inspection confidence in real time.

Beyond defect detection, the platform performs intelligent batch-level analytics by identifying defect trends, highlighting recurring quality issues, generating automated inspection reports, and providing actionable insights for quality engineers. By integrating zero-shot AI, explainable visual intelligence, historical defect memory, and immersive 3D visualization into a unified platform, OmniInspect AI reduces manual inspection effort, minimizes retraining costs, improves production efficiency, and enables scalable intelligent automation for modern Industry 4.0 manufacturing.

Project Title: Silicohelp
Problem Statement: Silicosis is an incurable, preventable lung disease affecting workers in India's stone quarries, mines, and construction sites. It is legally recognized as a compensable occupational disease under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, and the Supreme Court (PRASAR v. Union of India, 2024 INSC 582) has ordered certification and ₹3 lakh compensation per affected worker. Yet over 80% of India's workforce is informal, silicosis is routinely misdiagnosed as tuberculosis, and most affected workers are illiterate, non-digital-native, and have no employer record proving they were ever exposed. As a result, compensation that is legally owed almost never reaches the worker who earned it — and the very people the law protects are the least equipped to navigate the system meant to help them.
Project Description:
A worker in an unregistered stone-crushing unit breathes silica dust for years and eventually falls seriously ill. By law, he's entitled to ₹3 lakh in compensation. In practice, he rarely receives it — his illness often gets recorded as tuberculosis, his employer never registered him anywhere, and there's no paper trail connecting his sickness to his job. Even where digital systems exist (like Rajasthan's AI-assisted silicosis portal, launched in 2019), the government's own data shows only 1.5% of registered living patients and 16.6% of registered death cases have actually received payout. The gap isn't diagnosis — it's proof, access, and follow-through.
Why existing efforts fall short:
Peer-reviewed research confirms that most Indian states officially notify very few silicosis cases, largely because there's no centralized system connecting a worker's exposure history to their diagnosis to their legal claim. And any system built to close that gap has to work for people who may not read, may not own a smartphone comfortably, and speak dozens of different languages — a constraint most digital health tools ignore.
What we're building:
An end-to-end platform that takes a worker from first contact to compensation payout, designed specifically around the realities of who this worker actually is:
Registration, built for real users, not ideal users
Dual registration: a worker can self-register, or a hospital/NGO/health camp can register on their behalf
Aadhaar OCR auto-fills name, age, gender, address, and Aadhaar number — no manual typing, critical for illiterate users and reducing errors
Full multi-language support (Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, English, and extensible)
Voice-guided navigation reads out every instruction and accepts spoken answers, so literacy is never a barrier to registering
Turning work history into evidence
Captures workplace, job type, years worked, daily dust exposure, and safety equipment used
Calculates an Occupational Exposure Score (e.g., 92/100 – Very High Exposure) — giving doctors a single, standardized risk indicator instead of raw, hard-to-interpret history
AI-assisted, doctor-verified diagnosis
Chest X-ray upload via camera, gallery, or hospital digital copy
AI flags Low / Medium / High risk to prioritize doctor review
Explainable AI: instead of a black-box risk label, the app shows specific findings (e.g., "lung nodules detected," "upper lobe opacity") with a confidence score, plus a heatmap highlighting the exact regions the AI focused on
A registered doctor always makes the final call — approving or rejecting the AI's assessment — and digitally signs the report to prevent tampering. The AI supports the doctor; it never replaces them.
From certified diagnosis to compensation, automatically
Automatic claim generation: compensation form, medical report, and worker details are compiled into a single application with no repeated form-filling
Automatic submission to the Labour Department once the doctor verifies the case
Real-time claim tracking through every stage: Registration → Doctor Review → Submitted → Under Verification → Approved → Compensation Released
SMS notifications at each milestone, so a worker always knows where their claim stands — even without ever opening the app again
Built for where these workers actually live and work
Offline mode: the app functions without internet at remote quarry sites, storing data locally and syncing automatically once connectivity returns
Smart document validation catches blurry or unusable uploads before submission, avoiding rejected claims down the line
Fraud detection flags duplicate Aadhaar numbers, multiple claims, or suspicious documents
Oversight for the people managing this at scale
A Government Dashboard giving Labour Departments real-time visibility into total workers registered, high-risk cases, doctor-approved cases, and claim status across the board
A Worker Dashboard where each worker can privately view their profile, documents, AI report, and claim status
Centralized digital records keeping worker details, medical reports, AI results, doctor verification, and claim history in one secure, auditable place
Who this helps:
Illiterate and non-digital-native informal workers who were previously excluded by design from digital health and legal systems; doctors and Labour Departments who need standardized, trustworthy documentation to act quickly; and NGOs/health camps who currently reconstruct this evidence by hand, if at all.
What makes this different:
AI chest X-ray screening for silicosis already exists commercially (Qure.ai), and Rajasthan has already piloted an AI-linked certification portal. Neither solves accessibility for illiterate, non-smartphone-fluent workers, neither works offline, and neither automatically converts a certified diagnosis into a submitted, tracked compensation claim. This project is the missing layer connecting a law that already exists to the workers it was written to protect — built around their actual literacy, language, connectivity, and documentation constraints, not around the assumption that they can navigate a government portal themselves.

Project Title: MCP Guardian: A Real-Time Security Firewall That Protects AI Agents from Prompt Injection, Tool Poisoning, and Data Leaks
Problem Statement: AI agents are no longer just chatbots. They now connect to files, databases, and outside tools using a standard called the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and that opens up two weak spots. First, a tool the agent trusts can be tampered with to hide secret instructions inside a normal-looking response, quietly hijacking what the agent does. This is known as prompt injection or tool poisoning. Second, a user's own prompt can accidentally send private information or unsafe content straight into the AI. Most security tools today only check the user's input, or they scan the setup once and produce a report. Nobody is watching the live conversation and stopping an attack the moment it happens. That is the gap we set out to close.
Project Description:
MCP Guardian is a real-time security firewall that sits quietly in the middle of the conversation between the user, the AI agent, and its tools. Think of it as a bodyguard that checks every message going in both directions before it ever reaches the AI.

On the user side, it scans prompts for private information using Microsoft Presidio and for toxic or unsafe content using Detoxify. On the tool side, it inspects every tool response for hidden instructions, disguised payloads, and unexpected data patterns. A fast first check catches the obvious cases instantly, and anything suspicious is passed to a smarter AI judge that gives it a risk score from 0 to 100, names the type of attack, and explains its reasoning in plain language.

Every message then gets one of four clear verdicts: Allow, Sanitize, Quarantine, or Block. A live dashboard stays calm and green while everything is safe, and flips to a full red alert the instant an attack is caught, showing exactly what happened and why. As a bonus feature, an Attack Propagation Graph shows how far the attack could have spread if we had not stopped it.

What makes Guardian different is timing. Existing MCP security tools only scan once and hand you a report to read later. Guardian watches continuously and blocks live attacks while the conversation is still happening. It is built with FastAPI, WebSockets, the MCP SDK, Presidio, Detoxify, Sentence-Transformers, and Groq, and it runs fully offline and free. In our live demo, judges can try to sneak in a poisoned document or a private data prompt, and watch Guardian catch it in real time.

Project Title: A Smart 360° Pesticide Spraying Robot for Plant Health Monitoring
Problem Statement: Traditional manual pesticide spraying exposes farmers to toxic chemicals, causes chemical waste through uneven distribution, and lacks continuous plant health tracking. This creates a critical need for an automated solution to protect human health, optimize resources, and improve early disease detection
Project Description:
A Smart 360° Pesticide Spraying Robot for Plant Health Monitoring 

The Smart 360° Pesticide Spraying Robot is an intelligent agricultural rover designed to improve farming efficiency by combining precision pesticide spraying, real-time plant health monitoring, and autonomous navigation. Unlike conventional pesticide sprayers, this rover can be controlled directly through a mobile application using the ESP32's Wi-Fi capability, eliminating the need for expensive joysticks or dedicated remote controllers, making it a highly cost-effective solution for small and marginal farmers.

The humidity sensor measures field moisture to assist in better spraying decisions, and the small display provides live system information such as battery level, spraying status, and sensor readings.

By integrating this rover with a mobile application, farmers can track the rover's live location, monitor field operations, receive plant health updates, and control spraying remotely, significantly reducing labor costs, saving time, improving crop productivity, and enabling smart precision farming.

Problem Statement:
Millions of visually impaired individuals struggle to navigate unfamiliar environments safely and independently. Existing solutions like white canes and guide dogs primarily detect nearby obstacles but cannot provide contextual information such as identifying objects, people, pathways, or potential hazards. This lack of real-time environmental awareness limits mobility, confidence, and personal safety.
Our goal is to build an AI-powered wearable assistant that captures live surroundings through a wearable camera, analyzes the scene using a Vision-Language Model running on a Raspberry Pi, and delivers real-time contextual audio guidance through bone-conduction headphones, enabling users to navigate more safely while remaining aware of ambient sounds.
Project Description:
Our project is an AI-powered wearable assistant designed to improve the independence and safety of visually impaired individuals. The system uses a wearable camera to capture the user's surroundings in real time and processes the video on a Raspberry Pi using OpenCV and a Vision-Language AI model. The AI understands the environment by identifying objects, obstacles, people, stairs, and movement, then generates contextual descriptions.
These descriptions are instantly converted into speech using a Text-to-Speech engine and delivered through bone conduction headphones, enabling users to receive guidance while remaining aware of ambient sounds. Unlike traditional navigation aids, our solution provides intelligent scene understanding rather than simple object detection, allowing users to make informed decisions about their surroundings.
The device is lightweight, portable, and suitable for both indoor and outdoor environments. It offers features such as real-time obstacle alerts, context-aware narration, direction-based guidance, and wearable accessibility support. By combining computer vision, edge AI, and audio assistance, this project aims to make navigation safer, smarter, and more accessible for people with visual impairments.
Tech Stack: Raspberry Pi, Python, OpenCV, Vision-Language Model (Moon dream2/Phi-3 Vision), Text-to-Speech (TTS), Bone Conduction Headphones.

Project Title: Credential & Secret Leak Prevention in AI-Generated Code
Problem Statement: AI coding assistants frequently generate code that hardcodes API keys, tokens, or example credentials copied from training patterns, risking accidental exposure when committed to public repos.
Project Description:
Problem: AI coding assistants often generate hardcoded secrets (API keys, tokens, placeholder credentials). Existing scanners (GitLeaks, TruffleHog) only catch known key formats — they miss AI-specific patterns, like a placeholder (YOUR_API_KEY_HERE) later swapped for a real value.
Solution: A pre-commit/CI tool that:

Detects AI-boilerplate placeholder patterns in code
Flags when a placeholder gets replaced with a high-entropy "real-looking" value
Scores risk based on file type + entropy, not just regex match
Suggests auto-fix (move secret to .env + .gitignore)

Tech stack: Python, entropy scoring, pre-commit hook framework, optional GitHub Action.

Project Title: Toxic air cleaner
Problem Statement: Modern urban living has led to significant declines in indoor air quality (IAQ) due to poor ventilation, synthetic construction materials, and the accumulation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and fine particulate matter (PM_{2.5}). Traditional mechanical air purifiers are often energy-intensive, rely on disposable, non-recyclable synthetic filters, and fail to regulate indoor humidity or CO$_2$ levels. There is an urgent need for a sustainable, energy-efficient solution that combines high-efficiency mechanical filtration with biological air purification to create healthier living environments.
Project Description: The EcoFlow project aims to develop a dual-stage, modular air purification system designed specifically for apartments and small office spaces. The system integrates traditional high-efficiency filtration with a controlled botanical component to maximize air quality improvement.

Project Title: Lief guard
Problem Statement:
Athletic progress depends entirely on the balance between intense training strain and proper nutritional recovery.
The Problem
Overtraining & Injury Risks: Pushing through severe muscular and neural fatigue leads to chronic exhaustion, muscle tissue breakdown, and severe injuries.
The Data Disconnect: Existing smartwatches only track passive metrics (like steps), completely failing to measure weightlifting intensity. Meanwhile, nutrition apps require tedious manual text entry, causing most athletes to quit tracking.
Delayed Feedback: Athletes have no real-time system to warn them during a workout when their muscular output is dropping due to under-fueling.
Project Description:
How It Works
The Wearable (IoT Node): An ESP32 microcontroller uses an accelerometer (MPU6050) and a heart rate sensor (MAX30102) to measure active lifting velocity and cardiovascular strain. A built-in OLED screen and Buzzer provide instant visual and auditory safety alerts right on the gym floor.
The Workout Logger (Web App): Users log their specific daily routine (e.g., Heavy Leg Day) in a web app, which uses sports science logic to automatically scale up their baseline macronutrient and calorie targets.
Frictionless Nutrition (RFID Tags): To eliminate manual typing, athletes carry labeled RFID keycards (e.g., "Protein Shake"). Tapping a card against the device instantly updates their nutrition intake via a Firebase Cloud Database

Project Title: Cross-Channel "Mule Account" Detection Graph and Management
Problem Statement: As online banking expands quickly, criminals rely on mule accounts to route stolen funds through several banking pathways, which makes tracking far harder. Many current anti-fraud tools do not reliably spot these multi-channel transfers as they happen. What’s required is an intelligent approach that flags questionable flows sooner, uncovers mule-account rings, and supports banks in stopping monetary fraud before damage is done.
Project Description:
On a daily basis, banks handle countless transfers via mobile apps, UPI, online portals, digital wallets, and ATM networks. Criminals take advantage of this flow by routing illicit funds through many different accounts, often called mule accounts, which makes following the trail challenging. Because the movement occurs in minutes and spans several channels, older detection tools frequently miss the full shape of the fraud.
In our initiative, the Cross-Channel Mule Account Detection and Management System, all of these activities are unified within one smart platform. When accounts, devices, wallets, and payments are linked into a connected network, the platform can spot questionable fund flows as they occur. Each transfer receives a risk rating, bank teams are notified right away, and a visual view of the scheme is offered to ease investigative work.
With AI-driven analysis and graph-oriented fraud detection, this approach enables banks to spot scams sooner, limit monetary damage, shield customers from deception, and reinforce confidence in digital banking.

Project Title: Revora – A Smart Recycling and Waste Collection Platform
Problem Statement:
People, apartments, restaurants, shops, and industries often have recyclable waste, but they don't know:
Who can collect it.
Whether it has value.
Where to send it.
As a result, recyclable waste ends up in landfills.

Project Title: StockSentinel:AI Market Threat Detection & Stock Intelligence Platform
Problem Statement: Retail investors often rely on delayed or fragmented information from stock prices, financial news, social media, and earnings calls, making it difficult to identify market threats such as manipulation, insider trading, panic selling, and sudden market crashes. This lack of real-time intelligence can lead to poor investment decisions and significant financial losses.
Project Description:
StockSentinel is an AI-powered financial intelligence platform that predicts stock price trends while proactively detecting market threats using machine learning and natural language processing. The system analyzes live stock prices, trading volumes, financial news, social media sentiment, and company financial reports to identify risks such as pump-and-dump schemes, insider trading, market manipulation, and panic selling.

A unique feature of the platform is the Earnings Call Intelligence Module, which automatically transcribes earnings calls, generates concise summaries, detects bullish and bearish signals, analyzes CEO/CFO sentiment, compares tone with previous quarters, and extracts key financial insights. These analyses are combined into a unified AI Risk Score and presented through an interactive dashboard with real-time alerts and explainable recommendations, enabling investors to make faster, smarter, and more informed investment decisions.

Project Title: ARISE - Autonomous Robot for Intelligent Suspended Extraction
Problem Statement: Tea plantations in hilly regions continue to rely heavily on manual harvesting, leading to labor shortages, high operational costs, inconsistent plucking quality, and reduced productivity. The challenging terrain also limits the use of conventional agricultural machinery, creating a need for an intelligent, scalable, and terrain-adaptive harvesting system that can automate tea leaf collection while maintaining quality and improving efficiency.
Project Description: ARISE (Autonomous Robot for Intelligent Suspended Extraction) is a cable-driven robotic harvesting system designed specifically for tea plantations in hilly terrain. The system uses four support poles connected by steel cables, allowing a suspended robotic pod to move in the X, Y, and Z directions. Using AI-based vision, the pod identifies tender tea leaves (two leaves and a bud), harvests them, and transfers them through a suction mechanism into a collection bag. Once the bag is full, the robot transports it to the nearest support pole for collection and continues harvesting. Multiple interconnected cable sectors enable the robot to move across large plantations, while a smart dashboard supports both autonomous operation and manual control, making the system efficient, scalable, and suitable for large-scale tea estates.

Project Title: Smart IV Infusion Monitoring and Intelligent Nurse Assistance System.
Problem Statement: Intravenous (IV) infusion monitoring in hospitals is still largely dependent on manual observation. Nurses are often responsible for monitoring multiple patients simultaneously, making it difficult to continuously track IV fluid levels. As a result, IV bottles may not be replaced promptly, leading to interruptions in infusion therapy, increased workload for healthcare staff, and reduced operational efficiency. Existing monitoring practices also make it challenging to manage multiple IV infusions simultaneously and ensure timely intervention in busy hospital environments.
Project Description: IoT-enabled IV infusion monitoring system designed to assist healthcare professionals in monitoring IV bottles more efficiently. The system uses a load cell sensor and ESP32-S3 to continuously measure the remaining IV fluid and calculate the fluid percentage in real time. The monitored data is displayed on an OLED display and a Blynk dashboard, allowing healthcare staff to monitor multiple IV units remotely. When the IV fluid reaches predefined thresholds, audible (buzzer and voice), and mobile notifications to ensure timely bottle replacement.

Project Title: MetalliSense – AI-Powered Alloy Optimization for Sustainable Smart Foundries
Problem Statement: Foundries rely on manual alloy correction, resulting in material waste, high energy consumption, re-melting, inconsistent quality, and increased production costs. Despite having real-time process data, most industries lack AI-powered decision support to optimize alloy composition and improve sustainable manufacturing.
Project Description: MetalliSense is an AI-driven smart manufacturing platform that analyzes real-time spectrometer data to generate explainable alloy correction recommendations. By combining machine learning, industrial data integration, and human-in-the-loop decision-making, it helps foundries reduce material waste, energy consumption, re-melting cycles, and operational costs while improving product quality, production efficiency, and supporting Industry 4.0 and ESG goals.

Project Title: Decentralized  Mesh Communication Network
Problem Statement: During disasters, communication infrastructure such as mobile towers and internet services often fails, delaying rescue efforts. Victims and responders struggle to exchange critical information and locations. Existing communication systems rely heavily on centralized networks, making them unreliable during emergencies. There is a need for a scalable, infrastructure-free communication solution that works anywhere. ResiliMesh addresses this challenge with a decentralized LoRa mesh network for reliable emergency communication.
Project Description: ResiliMesh is a decentralized communication system designed for disaster and emergency situations. It uses ESP32 and LoRa SX1278 to create a self-healing mesh network without internet or cellular connectivity. Each node can send, receive, and relay messages while automatically joining the network. The system supports GPS-based SOS alerts, short voice messaging, and multi-hop communication. A web dashboard provides live monitoring of nodes, locations, and emergency events.

Project Title: Snap-In-Voice: Bill, EMI and Debt Risk Management Platform
Problem Statement:
Individuals frequently manage multiple utility bills, credit-card payments, BNPL dues and digital-loan EMIs across different applications. Important information such as processing fees, annual percentage rate, net disbursed amount, penalty charges and repayment dates is often difficult to understand or scattered across multiple documents.

Existing bill-reminder applications primarily notify users about due dates but do not analyse whether the user can afford a new loan, identify overlapping repayment obligations or calculate the true cost of borrowing. As a result, users may miss payments, accept high-cost loans and enter repeated borrowing cycles.

There is a need for an intelligent financial-management system that can extract bill and loan information, consolidate repayment obligations, calculate actual borrowing costs, predict repayment risk and generate a prioritised payment plan.
Project Description:
BillAxis is an intelligent financial obligation and debt-risk management platform that helps users understand, organise and repay their bills, credit-card dues and digital loans.

Users can upload loan Key Fact Statements, credit-card bills, utility bills or manually enter payment details. The system extracts important information such as sanctioned amount, net amount received, processing fees, interest rate, annual percentage rate, EMI amount, due dates and late-payment penalties.

BillAxis consolidates all obligations into a unified dashboard and calculates the user’s total monthly repayment burden. Its affordability engine compares monthly income, essential expenses, available balance and upcoming payments to generate a repayment-risk score.

Before a user accepts a new loan, BillAxis evaluates its actual cost and shows whether the repayment is affordable. It can also compare multiple loan offers using net disbursal, total repayment, APR, processing fees and penalties instead of comparing only the advertised interest rate.

The platform generates a prioritised repayment plan, sends due-date alerts and warns users about overlapping EMIs, high-cost borrowing and possible cash-flow shortages. BillAxis is designed to improve financial awareness and help individuals avoid missed payments and repeated debt cycles.

Project Title: Digital Will AI: Secure Digital Asset Inheritance Platform
Problem Statement:
In today's digital world, individuals own valuable online assets such as cloud storage, social media accounts, digital wallets, subscriptions, and important documents. When a person dies or becomes permanently incapacitated, trusted family members often cannot access these assets securely. Existing solutions mainly store passwords and lack intelligent, policy-based, and secure digital inheritance mechanisms.

Develop an AI-assisted cybersecurity platform that enables users to securely manage their digital assets, define trusted beneficiaries, and automate emergency access through encrypted policies while preventing unauthorized access and protecting user privacy.
Project Description:
Digital Will AI is an AI-powered cybersecurity platform that provides a secure digital inheritance solution for managing online assets. Users can register their digital accounts, organize important documents, assign trusted beneficiaries, and define customized access policies for emergency situations.

The platform secures all data using encryption and multi-factor authentication. During an emergency, AI assists in validating access requests, checking for suspicious activities, and ensuring that only authorized beneficiaries receive access according to the owner's predefined rules. The system also maintains detailed audit logs and provides risk analysis to protect against fraud and unauthorized access.

By combining AI with secure access control, Digital Will AI offers a modern approach to safeguarding digital assets and ensuring a safe, transparent, and privacy-preserving transfer of digital ownership.

Project Title: SecLens Vault
Problem Statement:
Developers and organizations rely on hundreds of API keys, access tokens, and cloud credentials to build modern applications. These secrets are often stored in environment files, configuration repositories, or local systems, making them vulnerable to accidental exposure, insider threats, and credential theft.

Traditional secret management solutions primarily focus on securely storing credentials, but they often provide limited visibility into how secrets are used after retrieval. As a result, malicious activity such as credential misuse, replay attacks, or unauthorized access may remain undetected until significant damage has already occurred.

The challenge is to build a secure credential management platform that not only protects sensitive secrets but also actively detects suspicious usage, maintains tamper-evident audit records, and enables developers to verify sensitive operations without exposing confidential information.
Project Description:
SecLens Vault is an intelligent credential management platform designed to secure, monitor, and validate the lifecycle of sensitive developer secrets.

The platform encrypts API keys and credentials at rest, issues short-lived access tokens for controlled usage, continuously monitors credential activity using deterministic security rules, and automatically responds to suspicious behavior through rapid security workflows.

Key capabilities include:

Secure Credential Storage
Encrypts all stored credentials using industry-standard cryptography.
Prevents plaintext exposure during normal operations.
Behavior-Based Threat Detection
Detects suspicious activities such as:
Replay attacks
Unusual request bursts
Geographic anomalies
Decoy credential access
Immediately triggers protective actions when malicious behavior is detected.
Automatic Incident Response
Revokes compromised sessions.
Rotates encryption material.
Records every security event for forensic analysis.
Tamper-Evident Audit Trail
Every operation is recorded in an append-only audit log.
Cryptographic integrity checks make unauthorized modifications detectable.
Zero-Knowledge Verification
Generates cryptographic proofs that allow verification of knowledge of a protected credential without revealing the credential itself.
Demonstrates privacy-preserving authentication using modern zero-knowledge techniques.
Real-Time Security Dashboard
Visualizes credential usage.
Displays live attack flows.
Shows security alerts and automated responses in real time.

Project Title: EduHive: Transforming Individual Learning into Collective Knowledge
Problem Statement:
Students today rely on multiple disconnected platforms such as YouTube, Reddit, Stack Overflow, Discord, and search engines to find academic
resources. While these platforms contain valuable information, they often lack structure, credibility, and context specific to a student's course or
curriculum. As a result, students spend significant time searching for reliable explanations instead of learning.
There is a need for a unified platform that combines collaborative discussions, trusted educator contributions, and curated learning resources in
one organized academic space.
Project Description:
EduHive is a collaborative learning platform designed to transform scattered educational discussions into organized and trustworthy knowledge.
The platform enables students to ask academic questions, share explanations, and collaboratively build learning resources within subjectspecific communities.
To improve the credibility of information, verified educators can contribute authoritative explanations that are clearly distinguished from peer
responses. EduHive also curates relevant learning resources and recommends content based on community interactions, helping students
discover materials that have proven useful to others studying similar subjects.
Rather than replacing existing educational resources, EduHive acts as a centralized hub where discussions, explanations, notes, and learning materials are organized for efficient and collaborative learning.

Project Title: CrimeLens: AI-Powered Hotspot Intelligence & SOS Safety Platform for Proactive Policing
Problem Statement: Law enforcement agencies struggle to allocate limited patrol resources effectively because crime data (FIR/CCTNS) and accident data (IRAD) remain siloed, unstructured, and reactive rather than predictive. Police typically respond after incidents occur, with no unified system to identify high-risk zones in advance, understand time-based crime patterns, or dynamically optimize patrol coverage. Additionally, there is no integrated real-time emergency response mechanism for women's safety that connects directly to this intelligence layer, leaving a critical gap between data insight and on-ground protective action.
Project Description: CrimeLens is an AI-driven analytics platform that transforms raw FIR (CCTNS) and IRAD accident records into actionable safety intelligence. Using spatio-temporal clustering and time-series forecasting, the system identifies emerging crime and accident-prone zones and visualizes them through GIS-based, color-coded heatmaps. Multi-parameter filters (time, location, incident type) let officers drill into specific patterns, while an AI-driven patrol route optimizer helps allocate limited resources to the highest-need areas at the right times. A built-in Women Safety SOS module provides live location tracking and instant alert routing to the nearest patrol unit, closing the gap between data insight and real-world response. Every model output is paired with a bias-check layer to ensure recommendations don't reinforce existing patrol biases, making the system both effective and equitable. Built on cloud infrastructure with web and mobile dashboards, CrimeLens is designed to integrate directly with existing police control systems and scale from city to state level.

Project Title: Aegix AI autonomous AI security anal
Problem Statement:
Modern organizations deploy multiple cybersecurity tools such as Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), SIEMs, and TLS monitoring solutions. These tools generate thousands of security alerts every day, many of which are isolated, repetitive, or lack context.  Security analysts must manually investigate these alerts, correlate events from different sources, identify the actual attack, predict the attacker's next actions, and decide on an appropriate response. This process is time-consuming and can delay incident response, allowing attackers to escalate their attacks and cause significant damage.
There is a need for an intelligent system that can automatically correlate security events, analyze incidents using AI, explain its reasoning, learn from previous incidents, predict attacker behavior, and recommend effective response actions to help security teams respond faster and more accurately.
Project Description:
Aegix AI is an Autonomous AI Security Analyst designed to assist Security Operations Center (SOC) teams by intelligently analyzing and correlating security alerts from multiple sources. Instead of treating endpoint, network, and TLS alerts as separate events, Aegix AI combines them into a single incident, enabling faster and more accurate threat investigation.
The system uses AI to summarize incidents, classify attack types, estimate severity, explain the reasoning behind its conclusions, and predict the attacker's next likely actions. It also maintains a memory of previous incidents, allowing it to identify similar attack patterns and improve investigation efficiency over time.
For demonstration purposes, a Red Team attack simulator generates realistic cybersecurity events such as suspicious PowerShell execution, port scans, SMB activity, and weak TLS configurations. These events are detected by monitoring agents and processed by a correlation engine before being analyzed by a locally hosted Large Language Model (Gemma via Ollama).
Finally, Aegix AI provides actionable response recommendations—such as isolating a host, blocking an IP address, or terminating a suspicious process—to help analysts respond quickly and effectively.

Patients must repeatedly register at different hospitals, while doctors cannot easily access previous treatment histories. Administrators also lack a centralized platform to manage appointments, doctors, pharmacy inventory, and hospital operations. This results in duplicated records, longer waiting times, inefficient resource utilization, and poor patient experience.
Project Description: Develop a centralized, role-based web platform that connects multiple hospitals through a Universal MR Number, enabling patients, doctors, and hospital administrators to securely access the services they need while maintaining privacy and data security.

Project Title: Smart Expiry Swap
Problem Statement: Millions of food products in supermarkets go unsold and expire every year, leading to significant food waste, financial losses for retailers, and reduced access to food for people in need. Most stores lack an intelligent system to identify at-risk products and take timely action before they expire.
Project Description: Smart Expiry Swap is an AI-powered software platform that helps supermarkets minimize food waste by monitoring products nearing their expiry dates. The system analyzes product information such as expiry date, inventory levels, and sales patterns to predict items at risk of remaining unsold. Based on these predictions, it recommends appropriate discounts to encourage quick sales or notifies partnered NGOs to collect edible surplus food before it expires. By combining AI-based decision support with automated alerts and food redistribution, the platform reduces waste, saves costs for retailers, and supports sustainable food management.

College Name: Sathyabama Institute of Science and technology
Project Title: FROSTIQ
Problem Statement: Conventional refrigerators do not provide real-time monitoring, early fault detection, or remote alerts for conditions such as food spoilage, prolonged door opening, abnormal temperature, and irregular power consumption. Existing smart refrigerator solutions are costly and limited to specific models. Therefore, there is a need for a universal, plug-and-play external IoT device that can monitor refrigerator health, provide real-time data visualization, generate mobile alerts, and enable predictive maintenance without modifying the refrigerator's internal hardware.
Project Description:
The IoT Smart Refrigerator Monitoring System is a universal monitoring device designed to enhance any conventional refrigerator without requiring modifications to its internal hardware or electronics. The device uses a standard ESP32 microcontroller and multiple sensors to continuously monitor key refrigerator parameters, including food spoilage indicators, internal temperature, door status, and power consumption.

The collected sensor data is transmitted to a cloud platform over Wi-Fi, where it is stored and synchronized with a mobile application. The mobile application provides real-time monitoring, historical data visualization through charts and graphs, and instant push notifications when abnormal conditions such as food spoilage, prolonged door opening, abnormal temperature, or unusual power consumption are detected. The system also analyzes power consumption patterns to identify potential refrigerator faults, enabling predictive maintenance before a complete failure occurs.

The proposed solution is affordable, portable, easy to install, and compatible with refrigerators of different brands and models, making it a practical IoT-based smart monitoring system for improving food safety, reducing energy waste, and minimizing unexpected appliance failures.
